findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain
findings.body: `translate` caches no-arg lookups under `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. With fallbacks, the result for a locale now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is not part of the key. If a key is missing in the user's locale, the cached value is the site-default or English text. When an admin changes `default_locale`, or the fallback locale is loaded later, the stale fallback string stays in the 300-entry LRU cache until it is evicted or the backend reloads.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in controller requests
findings.body: The translate accelerator loads translations lazily, per locale, and only for `config.locale`. `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Sidekiq jobs, mailers and rake tasks that use `I18n.with_locale` or set `I18n.locale` never load the fallback locales (site default and `:en`). In those contexts a missing translation will not fall back and renders as a 'translation missing' string. The loading should happen inside the I18n layer, for example in `translate`, rather than only in one controller filter.

findings.title: Fallback lookup hits SiteSetting on every translate and can fail without a database
findings.body: `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every lookup, including cache misses and calls with arguments. Each call runs `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` and allocates new arrays. If the DB or SiteSetting is not ready (assets precompile, migrations, early boot) or the setting is nil, any translation call raises. The fallbacks hash also now applies in development and test, because the per-environment `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines were removed and replaced by a global initializer. Consider guarding against a nil setting and caching the chain.

findings.title: Fallbacks module included into whatever backend class is active at load time
findings.body: `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` includes the module into whichever class the backend happens to be at initializer time. If the backend is a Chain or a plugin-provided class, fallbacks are silently not applied to `Simple`. The pluralization include targets `Simple` explicitly, so the two are inconsistent. Include into `I18n::Backend::Simple` explicitly.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
findings.body: The PR adds a custom fallback order (user locale, site locale, English), lazy loading of fallback locales, and `ensure_loaded!`. None of this has specs, for example a missing key in a non-English locale falling back to the site default or English, or `ensure_loaded!` loading the fallback locales.
